aerospace_defense.finishing_labor_note: Fatigue- and aero-critical surfaces need tight, traceable tolerances under AS9100/FAA oversight, so deburring, blending, and polishing stay manual instead of fixed-tooled.

aerospace_mro.name: Aerospace MRO

naics_codes.488190: Other support activities for air transportation

part_geometry_classes: large airframe skins and fuselage panels
aerospace_mro.finishing_labor_note: Airframe stripping, blasting, and repaint during scheduled maintenance is a major, recurring application done largely by hand under OEM paint specs; this segment is easy to miss because it's a services NAICS code, not a manufacturing one.

maritime.name: Maritime
maritime.finishing_labor_note: Corrosion protection in a saltwater environment demands heavy grinding, blasting, and coating prep over large, awkward hull surfaces that don't fit fixed cells.

naics_codes.336992: Military armored vehicle, tank, and tank component manufacturing

specialty_and_heavy_vehicles.finishing_labor_note: High-mix, low-to-mid volume production with cosmetic Class-A or mil-spec coating requirements keeps sanding and grinding manual rather than fixed-automated.

naics_codes.333924: Industrial truck, tractor, trailer, and stacker machinery manufacturing

heavy_equipment_and_machinery.finishing_labor_note: Parts exceed the reach and payload of typical fixed robotic cells, so weld grinding and deburring remain manual.

metal_fabrication.name: Metal fabrication

naics_codes.332323: Ornamental and architectural metal work manufacturing
naics_codes.332999: All other miscellaneous fabricated metal product manufacturing

metal_fabrication.finishing_labor_note: Extreme part variety and small lot sizes make fixed tooling uneconomical, so weld grinding and deburring stay manual job-shop work.
